newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAP MEANS SOMETHING EXTRA FOR CROFT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAP MEANS SOMETHING EXTRA FOR CROFT.

text.p: Playing cricket for England has always meant something extra for a Welshman. Glamorgan off-spinner Robert Croft is no exception.
"The way we look at it down here is like this," Croft reflected.
"When we're playing for Glamorgan in the county championship, we're representing our country, Wales.
"When we have the honour of being chosen for a test match for England, it's like being picked for the British Lions.
Croft, who turns 27 during the third one-day international against Australia at The Oval on Sunday, has long been talked about as a potential England player.
But he was unable to force his way in to the side until the final test against Pakistan last year, an experience which could have daunted a less resilient soul.
Pakistan, already one-up in the three-test series, merrily rattled up 521 in their first innings with opener Saeed Anwar making 176.
But while paceman Chris Lewis and leg-spinner Ian Salisbury went for four or five an over, Croft remained unruffled by the onslaught.
Plugging away with control, while still confident enough to vary his angles of flight and direction, Croft stuck to his task.
He finished with two for 166 from 47 overs and in the midst of a crushing defeat and the loss of the series 2-0, England had something positive.

Croft explained later that one his mentors, former England medium-pacer Tom Cartwright, had told him to stamp his feet on The Oval turf when he came out for his test debut just to ensure he realised he was not dreaming.
Cartwright recalled he had known Croft since he was "quite a fat kid" who never stopped talking.
But he is also prepared to listen, spending hours during the winter tour listening to another former England bowler, off-spinner John Emburey.
His figures so far in test cricket are encouraging.
He took eight wickets in the two tests against Zimbabwe, missed the drawn first test against New Zealand at Auckland before returning to play a full part in the following two test victories.
In the third test at Christchurch, Croft bowled with intelligence and guile, taking five for 95 from 39.1 overs. He also made useful 31 in England's first innings.
Just as importantly, Croft has displayed unbounding enthusiasm, as befits one whose entry in the Cricketers' Who's Who alongside 'Opinions on cricket' lists "enjoyment is of the utmost importance".
Croft is already rated by some observers as the best England off-spinner since Freddie Titmus, the little Middlesex off-spinner who last appeared for his country 22 years ago.
He has won selection in the England squad for the three-match one-day series starting at Headingley in Leeds on Thursday and is now regarded as the team's senior spinner.
The six-test Ashes series will prove the ultimate test for a Welshman whose future at the moment looks as rosy as the rugby team's national shirt.
